triggers.when: Writing, modifying, refactoring, or reviewing implementation code.
Writing, changing, or reviewing tests and fixtures.
Writing or revising technical documentation and delivery notes.
Fixing defects, regressions, or verification failures at their root cause.
Diagnosing a bug, failing check, or unexpected behavior before proposing a fix.
Making any completion, readiness, or handoff claim.
Staging changes, writing commit messages, or preparing pull request titles.
Preparing, opening, updating, or handing off a pull request.

clauses.guidance: Keep root agent instructions as short mandatory pointers. Setup owns only marked baseline content; preserve repository-authored bytes outside setup markers and keep project-specific architecture and policy in repository-owned documents.
Fix root causes.
Do not suppress diagnostics, weaken assertions, swallow errors, add timing hacks, or bypass a required check to produce a passing result.
Keep follow-up work outside the current slice; record it for later instead of expanding the active change.
Record the commands and outcomes that provide fresh evidence for every acceptance criterion.
Use fresh evidence from the current worktree before claiming work complete, fixed, passing, ready, committed, or delivered. A narrower check supports only the behavior it exercised.
Run the selected repository Verification before completion claims. Treat every failure as blocking and report the command plus its actionable diagnostic.

Do not edit verification configuration, tests, fixtures, golden files, or generated expectations merely to make a failure disappear. Change them only when the repository contract intentionally changes, and prove the new contract.
Stop and ask for explicit authority before intentionally changing lint, formatter, typecheck, test-runner, architecture, or Verification configuration.
Activate every matching required skill before governed work. When one skill has distinct active-module triggers, retain and follow each trigger.
Use the governing `conventional-commits` skill before staging changes, writing commit messages, or preparing pull request titles.
Use the governing `github-pr-workflow` skill before preparing, opening, updating, or handing off a pull request.
Write generated repository guidance, identifiers, headings, and examples in English. Preserve repository-authored language outside setup-owned markers.
For external APIs and libraries, use current authoritative documentation through the profile's declared documentation skill.
Search repository files with local code-search tools.
When authoritative documentation cannot answer an external question, use the profile's declared external web-research fallback with varied searches and verify conclusions against primary sources.
Do not use external research tools to discover or infer local repository code or behavior.

Use the repository's declared package manager and lockfile workflow. Add or upgrade a dependency only for a named job the existing stack cannot perform, and keep manifest and lockfile changes together.
Review every new dependency for necessity, provenance, maintenance, and security before delivery.
Inspect repository status before staging or delivery and preserve unrelated work.
Stop and ask for explicit authority before destructive Git operations that discard, overwrite, or remove work.
Stop and ask for explicit authority before committing, pushing, creating a branch, or opening a pull request when that authority is not already explicit.
Never guess a decision the user can answer cheaply. Ask through the available user-interaction tool, or ask plainly and stop when no such tool exists.

Never read, print, commit, or generate secrets. Keep credentials and environment-specific values in the repository's existing secure configuration boundary, and do not invent authentication, authorization, database, transport, or deployment policy.
